title: Give the checkout's own rule types their and, or and then

blocks.text: A web shop's checkout decides which parcels may ship next-day and what a parcel costs. The team declared its own `Rule` and `Adjustment` interfaces in `src/main/java/practice/Checkout.java`, so the code reads in the shop's words, but nobody has written their combining methods yet: `Rule.and`, `Rule.or` and `Adjustment.then` all throw.
Write those three methods. When you're done:

items: `nextDay()` turns down a parcel whose postcode is missing instead of failing on it;
every rule in a chain is asked at most once, in the order the chain was written, and only while the answer is still open, because some of the shop's rules call a slow address service;
`price(percentOff, courierFee)` charges the courier fee in full on top of the discounted goods.

cases.says: and accepts only when both rules accept, or when either does, and then chains two price steps
once this rule rejects a parcel, and() never asks the other rule, so a missing postcode is turned down instead of throwing
and() asks the rule it was called on first and the argument second
once this rule accepts a parcel, or() never asks the other rule
a.then(b) applies a first and b to its result, so the courier fee is added after the discount

origin.section: andThen Runs the Receiver First and compose the Argument First; and/or Stop Early

concepts: Predicate.and and or evaluate the receiver first and the argument only when the receiver hasn't decided the result, so a guard placed first protects the checks after it.
f.andThen(g) applies f and then g to its result; f.compose(g) applies g first.
